title: Introduction to spconform: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Conformal Prediction
text: spconform provides distribution-free, finite-sample prediction intervals spatial spatio-temporally dependent data relaxing standard exchangeability assumption. provides two foundational procedures: scp_geostatistical() point-referenced (geostatistical) data, implementing locally weighted split conformal prediction spatial (spatio-temporal) distance kernels. scp_areal() areal (lattice) data, implementing neighbourhood-weighted leave-one-conformal prediction based graph adjacency structures. diagnose() comprehensive multi-panel diagnostics: assessing marginal validity, Winkler Interval Score (WIS) sharpness, conditional coverage across spatial strata, boundary effects, Moran’s II spatial residual autocorrelation. procedures model-agnostic: can supply point predictor (e.g., Random Forest, Kriging, GAM, Splines, Neural Networks), spconform constructs finite-sample valid prediction intervals regardless model misspecification.

title: Introduction to spconform: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Conformal Prediction
text: illustrate workflow meuse river dataset (Pebesma Bivand 2005), classic environmental spatial benchmark.
code: library(sp) data(meuse)  coords <- as.matrix(meuse[, c("x", "y")]) coords_scaled <- scale(coords) y <- log(meuse$zinc)

title: Introduction to spconform: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Conformal Prediction
text: scp_geostatistical() accepts prediction function signature function(s_train, y_train, s_new):
code: pred_fun <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   df_tr <- data.frame(y = y_train, x1 = s_train[, 1], x2 = s_train[, 2])   df_new <- data.frame(x1 = s_new[, 1], x2 = s_new[, 2])   fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + I(x1 * x2), data = df_tr)   as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = df_new)) }

what: Fitting Locally Weighted Conformal Prediction Intervals
title: Introduction to spconform: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Conformal Prediction
text: split observations 70% training 30% independent testing, generating 90% prediction intervals (α=0.10\alpha = 0.10):
code: set.seed(42) n <- nrow(coords_scaled) train_idx <- sample(n, floor(0.70 * n)) test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(n), train_idx)  s_train <- coords_scaled[train_idx, ]; y_train <- y[train_idx] s_test  <- coords_scaled[test_idx, ];  y_test  <- y[test_idx]  out <- scp_geostatistical(   s_train = s_train,   y_train = y_train,   s0 = s_test,   pred_fun = pred_fun,   alpha = 0.10,   split = 0.50,   seed = 123 )  print(out) #> <spconform> geostatistical conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 90.0% #> Number of prediction points: 47 #>    pred lower upper #> 1 6.141 5.440 6.841 #> 2 5.559 4.804 6.314 #> 3 5.762 4.973 6.550 #> 4 6.614 5.826 7.402 #> 5 6.378 5.461 7.296 #> 6 5.818 4.900 6.735 #> ... (41 more) summary(out) #> spconform summary #> ------------------ #> Type:               geostatistical  #> Target coverage:    90.0%  #> Mean interval width: 2.0079  #> Median interval width: 2.1986  # Standard S3 methods for seamless integration with R workflows: head(predict(out, interval = "prediction")) #>           fit      lwr      upr #> [1,] 6.140641 5.439800 6.841483 #> [2,] 5.559277 4.804208 6.314346 #> [3,] 5.761763 4.973349 6.550176 #> [4,] 6.613941 5.825527 7.402354 #> [5,] 6.378492 5.461288 7.295695 #> [6,] 5.817680 4.900477 6.734883 head(residuals(out, y_true = y_test, type = "abs")) #> [1] 0.29420248 0.31752988 0.23630978 0.20706075 0.22137896 0.02005065 head(as.data.frame(out)) #>            x         y     pred    lower    upper    width #> 7  1.5554130 1.6559960 6.140641 5.439800 6.841483 1.401683 #> 11 1.5902637 1.4126166 5.559277 4.804208 6.314346 1.510139 #> 12 1.3771384 1.3324446 5.761763 4.973349 6.550176 1.576827 #> 17 1.0165678 1.4021179 6.613941 5.825527 7.402354 1.576827 #> 19 0.8315911 1.1568296 6.378492 5.461288 7.295695 1.834407 #> 23 0.9374835 0.9821691 5.817680 4.900477 6.734883 1.834407 plot(out, y_true = y_test)

title: Introduction to spconform: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Conformal Prediction
text: scp_areal() constructs distribution-free prediction intervals areal units (polygons, counties, grid cells) linked graph adjacency matrices:
code: # Aggregate Meuse observations onto a 6x6 spatial grid xbreaks <- seq(min(meuse$x), max(meuse$x), length.out = 7) ybreaks <- seq(min(meuse$y), max(meuse$y), length.out = 7)  meuse$cell_x  <- cut(meuse$x, xbreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_y  <- cut(meuse$y, ybreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_id <- (meuse$cell_y - 1) * 6 + meuse$cell_x  agg <- aggregate(log(zinc) ~ cell_id, data = meuse, FUN = mean) names(agg) <- c("cell_id", "y") cell_coords <- unique(meuse[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y")]) agg <- merge(agg, cell_coords, by = "cell_id") agg <- agg[order(agg$cell_id), ]  # Construct Rook/Queen graph adjacency matrix n_cells <- nrow(agg) adj <- matrix(0, n_cells, n_cells) for (i in 1:n_cells) {   for (j in 1:n_cells) {     if (i != j) {       dx <- abs(agg$cell_x[i] - agg$cell_x[j])       dy <- abs(agg$cell_y[i] - agg$cell_y[j])       if (dx <= 1 && dy <= 1) adj[i, j] <- 1     }   } }  # Run 80% Areal Conformal Prediction out_areal <- scp_areal(y = agg$y, adjacency = adj, alpha = 0.20, decay = 1.0) print(out_areal) #> <spconform> areal conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 80.0% #> Number of prediction points: 21 #>    pred lower upper #> 1 5.966 5.148 6.785 #> 2 5.749 4.854 6.643 #> 3 5.981 5.145 6.817 #> 4 5.502 4.608 6.396 #> 5 6.495 4.576 8.415 #> 6 5.934 5.116 6.752 #> ... (15 more) coverage_report(out_areal, agg$y) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.7619048 #>  #> $mean_width #> [1] 1.866613 plot(out_areal, y_true = agg$y)

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially and Spatio-Temporally Dependent Data
text: Standard conformal prediction assumes exchangeable data — assumption routinely violated spatial settings nearby observations similar distant ones. Existing R packages address either purely temporal dependence (conformalForecast, AdaptiveConformal) ..d./exchangeable data (conformalInference, conformalClassification, cfcausal), none provides documented, unit-tested, unified solution spatial data CRAN. spconform , knowledge, first R package offer conformal prediction spanning major spatial data structures optional spatio-temporal extension. Status: spconform v0.1.1 available CRAN. passed strict R CMD check ---cran 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes across Windows, macOS, Linux (R-devel & R-release). permanent, citable snapshot initial release archived Zenodo (DOI ).

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially and Spatio-Temporally Dependent Data
code: library(spconform) library(sp)  data(meuse) s <- as.matrix(meuse[, c("x", "y")]) y <- log(meuse$zinc)  # Any user-supplied point predictor pred_fun <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   fit <- lm(y_train ~ s_train[, 1] + s_train[, 2] +             I(s_train[, 1]^2) + I(s_train[, 2]^2))   cbind(1, s_new[, 1], s_new[, 2],         s_new[, 1]^2, s_new[, 2]^2) %*% coef(fit) }  # 90% locally weighted conformal intervals set.seed(123) idx <- sample(nrow(s), floor(0.7 * nrow(s))) out <- scp_geostatistical(s[idx, ], y[idx], s[-idx, ], pred_fun, alpha = 0.1)  print(out) #> <spconform> geostatistical conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 90.0% #> Number of prediction points: 47  coverage_report(out, y[-idx]) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.957 #> $mean_width #> [1] 2.21  # spconform objects support standard S3 methods: predict(out, interval = "prediction") #>   fit   lwr   upr #> 1 5.30  2.85  7.45 #> 2 5.12  2.70  7.32  # Extract residuals residuals(out, y_true = y[-idx], type = "abs")

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially and Spatio-Temporally Dependent Data
code: # Aggregate Meuse to a 6x6 grid (21 occupied cells) xbreaks <- seq(min(meuse$x), max(meuse$x), length.out = 7) ybreaks <- seq(min(meuse$y), max(meuse$y), length.out = 7) meuse$cell_x  <- cut(meuse$x, xbreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_y  <- cut(meuse$y, ybreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_id <- (meuse$cell_y - 1) * 6 + meuse$cell_x  agg <- aggregate(log(zinc) ~ cell_id, data = meuse, FUN = mean) names(agg) <- c("cell_id", "y") cell_coords <- unique(meuse[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y")]) agg <- merge(agg, cell_coords, by = "cell_id") agg <- agg[order(agg$cell_id), ]  # Build adjacency matrix (Queen contiguity) n_cells <- nrow(agg) adj <- matrix(0, n_cells, n_cells) for (i in 1:n_cells) {   for (j in 1:n_cells) {     if (i != j) {       dx <- abs(agg$cell_x[i] - agg$cell_x[j])       dy <- abs(agg$cell_y[i] - agg$cell_y[j])       if (dx <= 1 && dy <= 1) adj[i, j] <- 1     }   } }  # 80% neighbourhood-weighted conformal intervals out_areal <- scp_areal(agg$y, adjacency = adj, alpha = 0.2, decay = 0.5) coverage_report(out_areal, agg$y) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.81 #> $mean_width #> [1] 1.79

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially and Spatio-Temporally Dependent Data
code: library(mgcv) library(bmstdr)  data("nysptime") df <- nysptime[complete.cases(nysptime[, c("utmx", "utmy", "y8hrmax", "Day", "Month")]), ] df$day_idx <- ifelse(df$Month == 7, df$Day, 31 + df$Day)  s <- as.matrix(df[, c("utmx", "utmy")]) t <- df$day_idx s_3d <- cbind(s, t) y <- df$y8hrmax  # Spatio-temporal GAM predictor pred_fun_st <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   train_df <- data.frame(x = s_train[, 1], y = s_train[, 2],                          day = s_train[, 3], z = y_train)   fit <- gam(z ~ te(x, y, day, k = c(8, 8, 4)), data = train_df)   new_df <- data.frame(x = s_new[, 1], y = s_new[, 2], day = s_new[, 3])   as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = new_df)) }  set.seed(123) n <- nrow(s_3d) train_idx <- sample(n, floor(0.7 * n)) out_st <- scp_geostatistical(   s_train = s_3d[train_idx, ],   y_train = y[train_idx],   s0 = s_3d[-train_idx, ],   pred_fun = pred_fun_st,   t_train = t[train_idx],   t0 = t[-train_idx],   temporal_bandwidth = 5,   alpha = 0.1,   split = 0.5 )  coverage_report(out_st, y[-train_idx]) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.909 #> $mean_width #> [1] 41.7

title: Comprehensive Diagnostic Suite for Spatial Conformal Prediction Objects — diagnose
text: diagnostic suite performs five rigorous audits prediction intervals: Marginal Validity & Sharpness: Evaluates empirical coverage     \(\frac{1}{m}\sum \mathbf{1}(Y_i \C(s_i))\), mean/median interval width,     strictly proper Winkler Interval Score (WIS):     $$\text{WIS}_\alpha(l, u, y) = (u - l) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(l - y)\mathbf{1}(y < l) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(y - u)\mathbf{1}(y > u)$$ Conditional Spatial Stratification: Partitions 2D spatial domain     \(\text{n\_bins} \times \text{n\_bins}\) equal-area quadrants assesses local coverage. Convex Hull Boundary Proximity: Assesses whether edge-effect     extrapolations degrade coverage near boundary spatial domain. Spatial Autocorrelation (Moran's ): Evaluates whether prediction     miscoverages nonconformity scores exhibit residual spatial clustering via Moran's \(\). Score Distribution: Analyzes empirical quantiles normality/QQ structure.

title: Neighbourhood-Weighted Conformal Prediction for Areal (Lattice) Data — scp_areal
text: y Numeric vector observed responses, one per areal unit. X Optional numeric design matrix covariates (one row per areal unit); passed pred_fun supplied. May NULL purely spatial (neighbourhood-based) prediction. adjacency Square adjacency (contiguity) matrix describing neighbourhood structure among length(y) areal units. Non-zero entries treated neighbours (coerced binary). pred_fun function signature function(y_train, X_train, idx_train, idx_target, adjacency) returning single numeric point prediction areal unit indexed idx_target, fitted using training units idx_train. NULL (default), simple neighbourhood-mean predictor used (mean y_train target's graph neighbours, falling back global training mean target observed neighbours). alpha Miscoverage level; intervals target \(1-\alpha\) coverage. Default 0.1. decay Decay rate neighbourhood weights; see areal_neighbor_weights.

title: Neighbourhood-Weighted Conformal Prediction for Areal (Lattice) Data — scp_areal
text: Uses full leave-one-(jackknife-style) conformal scheme:   areal unit \(\), model fit units used   predict unit \(\); resulting nonconformity scores across   units combined graph-distance-weighted quantile specific   target unit, calibration set dominated   spatially/graph-proximate units rather treating units   exchangeable. effective neighbourhood weight target unit   vanishingly small (e.g., isolated unit neighbours),   procedure falls back unweighted quantile units   issues warning.

Implemented neighbourhood-weighted leave-one-conformal prediction areal (lattice) data (scp_areal()).
